Q: Using a select clause in a case expression A:

You should change the SELECT to a Scalar Subquery

SELECT 
   id 
   , COUNT(*)
   , (CASE WHEN id = (SELECT MIN(ID) FROM PARTICIPANTS_TABLE AS p
                      WHERE p.id = e.id)
        THEN 1 ELSE 0 
      END) AS participant 
FROM EVERYONE_TABLE AS e
GROUP BY id

But a basic rule I always follow is to avoid Scalar Subqueries in the Select list, in my experience they tend to have a bad optimization.

I would rewrite it to an Outer Join (imho this is a main reason why people write Scalar Subqueries, in most cases they simply hide an Outer Join):

SELECT 
   t1.id 
   , COUNT(*)
   , COUNT(t2.ID) AS participant 
FROM EVERYONE_TABLE AS t1
LEFT JOIN
  (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM PARTICIPANTS_TABLE) AS t2
ON t1.id = t2.id
GROUP BY t1.id

Plus I think this syntax is easier to understand.

Q: Catch NULL values using case expression A:

I've been trying to find a solution for Interbase / Firebird and this post kept popping up. None of the solutions here work because there is no ISNULL, so I figured I'd help anyone else who might come here looking for that:

select contactid, Title, FirstName, MiddleName,
    case coalesce(MiddleName, 'NULLVALUE')
    when 'R.' then 'Robert'
    when 'B.' then 'Bids'
    when 'J.' then 'John'
    when 'NULLVALUE' then 'New Name'
    else 'No Name'
    end, LastName
from Person.Contact

Q: Benefits of using a Case statement over an If statement in a stored procedure? A:

Don't concern yourself with any speed difference between a case expressions and an IF statement. Because you're dealing with a database, the amount of time it takes to write or read from disk is going to dwarf the time it takes the CPU to branch via an IF or Case. You should focus instead on which makes your code more readable and maintainable.

Q: Multiple Calculations in CASE expression A:

You are trying to calculate number1, number2 and number3 using a single CASE...WHEN...END statement, this will not work - you need 3 distinct case expressions.

If I understand your logic, this should do it

SELECT 
dbo.Table1.PrimaryKeyID,
  CASE
    WHEN (number1 >0 AND number2 = 0) 
       THEN number1 + CalcView.Quantity
    WHEN  (number1 =0 AND number2 >0) 
       THEN number1 + (CalcView.Quantity - number2)
    ELSE
       number1
  END AS number1,
  CASE 
    WHEN(number1 =0 AND number2 <=0) 
       THEN number2 - CalcView.Quantity
    WHEN  (number1 =0 AND number2 >0) 
       THEN 0
    ELSE
       number2
  END AS number2,
  CASE
    WHEN (number1 =0 AND number2 <=0) 
       THEN number3 + CalcView.Quantity
    WHEN  (number1 =0 AND number2 >0) 
       THEN number3 + number2 
    ELSE
       number3
  END AS number3
FROM Table1
INNER JOIN CalcViewON Table1.PrimaryKeyID= CalcView.PrimaryKeyID
WHERE Table1.PrimaryKeyID= CalcView.PrimaryKeyID

Q: Compare a date column versus a number of days from the current date using CodeIgniter's query builder A:

Try this:

$this->db
    ->where('status', '0')
    ->where("month >=", "CURDATE()", false)
    ->where("month <=", "current_date + interval '10' day", false)
    ->get('installments')
    ->result();
